analyst_view.overall: Manchester United are 19th with 8 points, and Mauricio Pochettino, who replaced the sacked Michael Carrick, lost 4-0 at Liverpool in his first game; this is his first home match. United play Sporting in Lisbon in the Champions League on Wednesday night, so they have barely three days to recover, while Sesko, Baleba and Ugarte are out and Rashford and Luke Shaw are doubts. Leny Yoro's red card at Anfield was overturned on 24 November, so he is available. Brentford are 6th after a 4-0 win over 10-man Everton but are without Igor Thiago (last game of a three-match league ban; Callum Wilson likely starts), Collins, Hickey, Henry, Milambo and Dasilva. The numbers now include Thiago's ban (about -10% on Brentford's goals) and the Sesko absence, so I no longer size those; Robert Jones referees, and his higher card rate is counted too.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals, 1.6 for United and 1.4 for Brentford, and they already count United conceding 19 in six games, Brentford's scoring and now Thiago's suspension. In my earlier view I took 6% off for Thiago because the numbers did not know about it; they do now, so that cut is gone. Yoro's return helps United's defence a little, and Wilson starting up front is a small step down for Brentford, so these roughly cancel out. I stay at about 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers expect 10.4 corners: 6.0 for United and 4.4 for Brentford, with recent form and past meetings already counted. Pochettino wants a front-foot United at home, which fits the home side winning most of the corners. Nothing in the team news changes that, so I stay at about 10.4.

cards.text: The numbers expect 4.4 cards. That already includes Robert Jones' above-average card rate (4.4 a game), United's rising card count and past meetings. A struggling side under a new manager could make it scrappy, but it is not a derby and there is no other clear reason to move, so I stay at about 4.4.

shots.text: The numbers expect 29.8 shots, 19.2 of them from United, with recent form counted. United play in Lisbon on Wednesday night and have little time to recover, and the numbers do not count that congestion. Thiago's ban is now in the numbers, so I only take about 3% off for United's tiredness, to about 28.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers expect 10.0 shots on target, including 4.1 for Brentford, helped by how many United have allowed lately. Thiago's absence is already counted now, so my earlier 5% cut is mostly gone. I keep a small 2% cut for United's tired legs after the Champions League trip, to about 9.8.
